meta.title: 1962 Canadian BCP, calendar and appointment rules
meta.description: The fixed calendar, the Year I and Year II rule, the lesson-table notes, the days of fasting and abstinence, the Ember and Rogation definitions, and the holy-day transfer rules, transcribed from the official ACC 1962 BCP.

sources.ref: The Book of Common Prayer (1962), General Synod of the Anglican Church of Canada, Calendar printed pages v to xii, Days of Fasting page xiii, notes to the Table of Lessons page xv, and General Rubrics before the Collects page 94
sources.note: Local copy /tmp/opencode/bcp1962-acc.pdf, text extracted with pdftotext -layout.

caveats: Commemoration names are transcribed verbatim, including bracketed entries which the witness prints in square brackets.
Rules are stored as verbatim text plus structured fields where the witness gives an explicit mapping.
The moveable-feast tables in the witness are 50-year reference tables, not an algorithmic definition. The app computes these values; the tables are not copied here.

yearRule.text: When the First Sunday in Advent occurs in a year with an even number, the Lessons appointed for the Year I shall be read, and when it occurs in a year with an odd number, the Lessons appointed for Year II shall be read, for the whole of that ecclesiastical year.

lessonTableNotes: When a Lesson begins with a pronoun, the reader shall substitute the appropriate noun.
In this Table, verses are stated inclusively.
Verses printed within brackets are permissive additions to the appointed passages.
The letter a after the number of a verse signifies the first part of that verse, and the letter b the second part.
fixedCalendarRule: When two lesser commemorations fall on the same day and it is desired to remember both, it is recommended that one of them be transferred to the nearest day before or after for which no special provision has been made.

daysOfAbstinence: All the Fridays of the Year except Christmas Day and the Epiphany

daysOfSolemnPrayer.definition: The Ember Days at the Four Seasons, being the Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday after the Third Sunday in Advent, the First Sunday in Lent, the Day of Pentecost (Whitsunday), and Holy Cross Day (September 14).
The Rogation Days, being the Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday before Holy Thursday, or the Ascension of our Lord.

transferRules.text: The Collect appointed for any Sunday or other Feast shall be used at the Evening Service next before, except in the case of Easter Day.
The Collect, Epistle, and Gospel of the Sunday shall serve all the week after, except when other provision is made.

On any weekday for which no special Collect, Epistle, and Gospel is appointed, the Priest may use the Collects, Epistles, and Gospels which are provided for lesser commemorations and weekdays, in accordance with the directions given on pages 309 and following.

The Collect appointed for any Holy-day may be said after the Sunday Collect during the seven days following; and the Collect, Epistle, and Gospel appointed for any Holy-day which has an Octave may be used on any day in the Octave for which no special provision has been made.

A Holy-day falling on a Sunday in Advent or Lent, or on Ash Wednesday or Ascension Day, shall be transferred to the following Tuesday. A Holy-day falling between Palm Sunday and Easter I shall be transferred to the Tuesday after Easter I; one falling between Whitsunday and Trinity Sunday shall be transferred to the Tuesday after Trinity Sunday. If any such Tuesday is not free, the Holy-day shall be transferred to some convenient day following.

cases.when: Sunday in Advent or Lent, Ash Wednesday, or Ascension Day
between Palm Sunday and Easter I

transferRules.text: But in the case of the Sundays after Christmas, Epiphany, and Trinity, and from Easter II to Easter V: the Collect, Epistle, and Gospel of the Holy-day shall be used, the Collect of the Sunday being said after the Collect of the Holy-day.

In the case of Holy-days falling on Septuagesima, Sexagesima, or Quinquagesima: the Service of the Purification of St Mary the Virgin shall be used on the Sunday, the Collect of the Sunday being said after that of the Feast; but the Conversion of St Paul, and St Matthias, shall be transferred to the following Tuesday.
Any Holy-day falling on a Monday (except the days from Christmas to Epiphany) may be transferred to the following Tuesday.

collectAscription: In reading any Collect ending with the words through Jesus Christ our Lord, the Priest may add the ascription who liveth and reigneth with thee and the Holy Spirit, one God, world without end.
